clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the far north of Finland above the Arctic Circle

source.quote: It is located in northern Finland north of the Arctic Circle within the Lapland region.

clues.text: This town sits in the far north of Finland, past the Arctic Circle. It lies in Lapland, the land at the top of the country.

clues.narrowing: narrows to far north places with weeks of summer daylight and no sunset

source.quote: The "midnight sun" is above the horizon from 29 May to 16 July, and the period with continuous daylight lasts a bit longer, polar night from 14 December to 29 December.

clues.text: Each summer, the sun here does not set at all for weeks. People call this long bright spell the midnight sun.

clues.narrowing: narrows to places whose council approved a Junttila coat of arms in 1963

source.quote: The coat of arms was designed by Einari Junttila, and was approved by the Kittilä municipal council at its meeting on 1 July 1963. The Ministry of the Interior confirmed the coat of arms for use on 26 November of the same year.

clues.text: Einari Junttila made this town's coat of arms. In 1963, the town council said yes to it, and the state said yes to its use that same year.

clues.narrowing: narrows to far north towns with a polar night that covers Christmas

source.quote: The "midnight sun" is above the horizon from 29 May to 16 July, and the period with continuous daylight lasts a bit longer, polar night from 14 December to 29 December.

clues.text: In late December, the sun does not rise here at all for days on end. Even Christmas Day comes and goes in the dark in this far north town.

clues.narrowing: confirms the town known for the national record low cold measured at Pokka

source.quote: Kittilä is famous for being the location of the lowest recorded temperature in Finnish history: −51.5 °C (−60.7 °F), measured in January 1999 in Pokka.

clues.text: This town is famous for the coldest air ever measured in its land. The record low was set at Pokka here in January 1999.
